messages:
elaine: Heads-up team procurement bulletin  brief policy tweaks rolling out today. Read the one-paragraph summary then the policy if you might be impacted: https://redwood.internal/finance/thresholds-update :link:

elaine: Summary bullets:
- Contractor hardware reimbursements now need pre-approval for any single purchase > $1,000 (was $500).
- P-card purchases for SaaS trials allowed up to $1,500 but require manager note in the expense.
- Any new vendor with expected recurring spend > $25k/year requires full onboarding (questionnaire + legal).
- "Fast-path" for one-off consultants and contractors under $9k: finance + PO only (no legal).

matt_g: Quick Q  is the $1,000 contractor hardware threshold per item or per checkout? Example: two monitors on one invoice for a contractor = $1,100.

elaine: Per invoice/receipt. If a single invoice > $1,000 we need pre-approval. If manager splits items across receipts we still look at intent; tag @people-ops if it's part of onboarding.

harry: We have a contractor who needs headset + monitor, invoice $950. That's under but includes a dock that might get ordered later. Any guidance?

elaine: Under $1k OK to reimburse post-hoc. If you expect subsequent purchases that push total >$1k during onboarding, submit contractor-equipment form ahead of time.

procure-bot: New vendor request logged: id=V-2026-2001, submitted by harry, est amount $950. Status: queued for finance ops.

sylvia: For recurring SaaS renewals that hover around $24k-26k, do we err on the side of questionnaire?

elaine: Yes please submit the vendor renewal form with projected ARR. Finance will classify risk; anything touching customer data or with SSO/OAuth integrations gets flagged for legal automatically.

matt_g: Is there an expedite process if hardware is needed for day-one access? Hiring start dates blocked otherwise.

elaine: Include the word "EXPEDITE" in the form and tag @finance. We'll aim to triage same-day and issue a provisional PO while onboarding completes. Managers should document the impact in the justification.

harry: Awesome, saving managers time. Will the one-page cheat-sheet be published?

elaine: Yep  we'll drop a 1-pager and a short post in #general with examples (contractor monitor, quick SaaS trial, one-off consultant). Expect that by EOD. Ping me or sylvia for edge cases. :sparkles:
